groups.title: Syrup (172836ASY)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for rheumatoid arthritis, juvenile rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis (degenerative joint disease), fever and pain caused by a cold, back pain, dysmenorrhoea, pain after surgery, ankylosing spondylitis, headache, toothache, muscle pain, neuralgia, acute gout, psoriatic arthritis, soft tissue injury (sprain, contusion) and non-articular rheumatic disease (tendinitis, tenosynovitis, bursitis).
groups.usage: For rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, soft tissue injury, non-articular rheumatic disease, acute gout and psoriatic arthritis, adults: take 200 to 600 mg per dose, 3 to 4 times in 1 day; up to 3200 mg may be taken in 1 day. For juvenile rheumatoid arthritis: take 30 to 40 mg per kg of body weight per dose, divided into 3 to 4 doses in 1 day. For mild to moderate pain and for a cold, adults: take 200 to 400 mg per dose, 3 to 4 times in 1 day. The dose may be increased or decreased appropriately according to age and symptoms. For children, ages 11 to 14 years: take 200 to 250 mg (10 to 12.5 mL) per dose; ages 7 to 10 years: take 150 to 200 mg (7.5 to 10 mL) per dose; ages 3 to 6 years: take 100 to 150 mg (5 to 7.5 mL) per dose; ages 1 to 2 years: take 50 to 100 mg (2.5 to 5 mL) per dose, 3 to 4 times in 1 day, and it is better to avoid taking it on an empty stomach. For children the maximum in 1 day is 1000 mg (50 mL) at ages 11 to 14 years, 800 mg (40 mL) at ages 7 to 10 years, 600 mg (30 mL) at ages 3 to 6 years and 400 mg (20 mL) at ages 1 to 2 years.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.

Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious and possibly fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration and perforation may occur.

People with uncontrolled high blood pressure, congestive heart failure, established ischaemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease or cerebrovascular disease must avoid high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day); people with cardiovascular risk factors (high blood pressure, high blood lipids, diabetes, smoking and the like) who need high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day) must consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, gastrointestinal ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, a severe blood disorder, severe liver impairment, severe kidney impairment, severe cardiac insufficiency or severe high blood pressure; if you have bronchial asthma; if you have had asthma, urticaria or an allergic reaction caused by aspirin or another anti-inflammatory analgesic; if pain occurs before or after coronary artery bypass surgery; if you are in the last 3 months of pregnancy; if you are breast-feeding; if you are being given high-dose methotrexate as cancer treatment; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Do not take more than the recommended dose.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have a blood disorder or a tendency to bleed; if you have liver cirrhosis, liver impairment or kidney impairment; if you have cardiac insufficiency or heart disease or high blood pressure; if you have systemic lupus erythematosus or mixed connective tissue disease; if you have ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease; if you are an older person; if the user is a child under 2 years of age; if you are pregnant; or if you have chickenpox.

When it is taken for a cold, as a rule this should be within 5 days; without the instruction of a doctor or pharmacist, do not take it for pain for 10 days or more (adults) or 5 days or more (children), and do not take it for fever for 3 days or more.

Do not take this medicine if you are being given high-dose methotrexate as cancer treatment, or together with another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are taking low-dose aspirin, an ACE inhibitor, lithium, furosemide or a thiazide diuretic, low-dose methotrexate, a coumarin anticoagulant (warfarin and the like) or a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: shock (difficulty breathing, a fall in blood pressure and the like); blood disorders such as reduced haematocrit, reduced haemoglobin, anaemia, aplastic anaemia, haemolytic anaemia, agranulocytosis, granulocytopenia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function or eosinophilia; peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, ulcerative colitis, bloody stools, gastritis, pancreatitis, vomiting of blood, Crohn's disease, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, upper abdominal pain, thirst, stomatitis, abdominal distension, mouth ulcers, constipation, black stools; Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis, drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms of unknown frequency, angioneurotic oedema, bullous dermatitis, erythema multiforme, maculopapular rash, reddening of the skin, blisters, rash, exfoliative dermatitis, acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis; hepatitis, jaundice, abnormal liver function, liver impairment; hypersensitivity or anaphylactic reactions, an asthma attack, urticaria, eczema, purple spots; visual disturbance, hearing loss, ringing in the ears, taste disturbance, vertigo, drowsiness, dizziness, depression, headache, a cerebrovascular event or nervousness; aseptic meningitis or meningitis (severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, a stiff neck, fever or disturbance of consciousness); acute renal failure, reduced urine output, blood in the urine, protein in the urine, raised BUN or blood creatinine, high blood potassium, interstitial nephritis, nephrotic syndrome, renal papillary necrosis, reduced urine volume, generalised oedema with breathlessness or lassitude; Conn's syndrome of unknown frequency; swelling around the eyes, swelling of the face, malaise, fever, nosebleed, swelling or peripheral oedema.

groups.usage: Adults: take 1 capsule (300 mg) per dose, 2 to 3 times in 1 day. When it is taken for an acute respiratory condition, do not take it continuously for 10 days or more.
groups.caution:
This medicine is not for people with hypersensitivity to it, liver cirrhosis, cystathionine synthase deficiency, peptic ulcer or severe kidney impairment (creatinine clearance below 25 mL/min).

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have mild or moderate liver impairment; if you have hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5; or if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding.

Headache, cold symptoms, difficulty breathing, taste disturbance, nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, upper abdominal pain, abdominal pain, heartburn, urticaria, erythema or eczema may occur.

groups.title: Soft Capsule (D22400ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills with shivering, fever, headache, joint pain, muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 2 capsules per dose. Ages 7 years to under 15 years: take 1 capsule per dose. Take it 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

If a severe skin adverse reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking it and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a baby (newborn) under 3 months of age; if you have severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure; or if you are 30 weeks or more pregnant.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a child under 2 years of age; if the user is a baby or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if symptoms of ischaemic colitis (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding and the like) appear in connection with pseudoephedrine; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma (for example eye pain or blurred vision) or difficulty passing urine; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive sputum, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. Drowsiness may occur after taking this medicine, so take care when driving or operating machinery. If symptoms do not improve after about 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with an antitussive-expectorant, another cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative, or an oral medicine containing an antihistamine (oral medicine for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicine, anti-allergy medicine). Do not take this medicine if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like) or have stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks. Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant, a steroid, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If rash and reddening of the skin, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema, difficulty passing urine, persistent or severe thirst, dizziness, anxiety, tremor or insomnia occurs, or if, rarely, anaphylactic shock (urticaria, swelling and chest tightness soon after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, a severe skin adverse reaction such as fever, erythema and many small pustules, asthma, general lassitude, jaundice (yellowing of the skin or the whites of the eyes) or interstitial pneumonia (cough, breathlessness, difficulty breathing, fever) occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

If symptoms of posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome or reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome (sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizure, visual disturbance and the like) occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

groups.title: Oral Suspension (271400ASS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for acute and chronic pain, gastritis, duodenal ulcer, oesophagitis, and stomach pain caused by digestive disturbance during radiotherapy.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1/2 to 1 sachet (1 sachet: 10 mL) per dose, 4 times in 1 day, swallowing it quickly.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you are on dialysis; if you are in the first 3 months of pregnancy; or if the user is a baby under 3 months of age or a child.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have had high blood magnesium or magnesium deficiency; if you have had kidney disease; if you have narrowing of the large bowel or acute appendicitis; or if you have kidney failure.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Swallow it quickly so that numbness in the mouth and the like does not remain. If symptoms do not improve after about 2 weeks of use, stop taking it and consult a pharmacist.

Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with digoxin, captopril, cimetidine, ranitidine, famotidine, theophylline, propranolol, atenolol, ferrous sulfate, chlorpromazine, acetylsalicylic acid, naproxen, metoprolol, levodopa, tetracycline, ciprofloxacin, ofloxacin, ketodeoxycholic acid, sodium fluoride, isoniazid, enoxacin, norfloxacin, levothyroxine or a coumarin derivative. Do not drink beverages immediately after taking it.

If diarrhoea, constipation, flatulence, skin rash, numbness, phosphate deficiency, dry mouth or taste disturbance occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist. Rarely headache, drowsiness, dizziness, weakness or accumulation of aluminium in nerve tissue and bone tissue may occur.

groups.title: Syrup (530800ASY)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the temporary relief of sneezing, runny nose, blocked nose and watering eyes caused by a cold or by allergic and vasomotor rhinitis, and of nasal congestion caused by sinusitis.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 12 years and older: take 10 mL every 4 hours, and do not exceed 60 mL in 24 hours. Ages 6 years to under 12 years: take 5 mL every 4 hours, and do not exceed 30 mL in 24 hours. For ages 2 years to under 6 years, follow the instructions of a doctor.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or to amine sympathomimetics or antihistamines; if you have an idiosyncratic constitution; if you are breast-feeding; if you have severe high blood pressure, severe coronary artery disease, narrow-angle glaucoma, urinary retention, peptic ulcer, asthma, emphysema or chronic lung disease; or if you are short of breath or have difficulty breathing.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have difficulty breathing such as chronic bronchitis, heart disease, high blood pressure, thyroid disease, diabetes, glaucoma or difficulty passing urine due to prostatic hyperplasia, or if the user is a child.

Take care when driving or operating machinery after taking it.

People taking an MAO inhibitor must not take this medicine. Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with a sedative or a tranquilliser. Avoid alcoholic drinks.

groups.title: Soft Capsule (142301ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for chronic polyarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, arthrosis, ankylosing spondylitis, painful swelling or inflammation after injury and surgery, and as an aid in the treatment of infections accompanied by inflammation, pain and fever.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 capsule (300 mg) per dose, 2 to 4 times in 1 day. Do not exceed 4 capsules (1200 mg) in 1 day.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.

Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious and possibly fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration and perforation may occur.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma, urticaria or an allergic reaction to aspirin or another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic; if you have gastrointestinal ulcer; if you have bleeding in the gastrointestinal tract, the cerebral blood vessels or elsewhere; if you have a severe blood disorder, severe liver impairment, severe kidney impairment, severe cardiac insufficiency or severe high blood pressure; if you have or have had bronchial asthma; if pain occurs before or after coronary artery bypass graft surgery (CABG); if you are 6 months or more pregnant; if you have inflammatory bowel disease such as Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis; or if you have had gastrointestinal bleeding or perforation.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have or have had a blood disorder; if you have a tendency to bleed; if you have or have had liver impairment or kidney impairment; if you have fluid retention or heart failure; if you have high blood pressure; if you have systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) or mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD); if you are an older person; if the user is a child aged 6 years or older; if you have stomach cancer or alcoholism; if you are in early or mid pregnancy or may be pregnant; if you have ischaemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease or cerebrovascular disease; if you have risk factors for cardiovascular disease (for example high blood pressure, high blood lipids, diabetes, smoking); if you have hepatic porphyria; if you have had major surgery with blood loss; if you have a blood clotting disorder; or if you have had a gastrointestinal ulcer caused by a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory medicine in the past.

Dizziness or fatigue may occur after taking this medicine, so take care when driving or operating machinery. When it is taken for a long period for an acute illness, as a rule this should be within 5 days.

Do not take it together with aspirin, another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic or high-dose methotrexate. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you take it together with a corticosteroid, alcohol, digoxin, phenytoin, probenecid, sulfinpyrazone, a sulfonylurea, an ACE inhibitor or angiotensin II receptor antagonist, a diuretic, lithium, a coumarin anticoagulant (warfarin and the like), baclofen, an immunosuppressant (ciclosporin, tacrolimus, sirolimus), a thrombolytic, ticlopidine, an antithrombotic, a medicine that raises blood potassium (for example a potassium-sparing diuretic, an ACE inhibitor, an angiotensin II receptor antagonist, an immunosuppressant such as ciclosporin or tacrolimus, trimethoprim or heparin), an inducer of CYP2C8 or CYP2C9 (for example rifampicin or phenobarbital), low-dose methotrexate (less than 15 mg a week), an antiplatelet medicine, a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor or low-dose aspirin.

groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.

Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious and possibly fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction and stroke, and serious cardiovascular adverse reactions may occur.

Taking this medicine may cause serious and possibly fatal gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as bleeding, ulceration and perforation of the gastrointestinal tract.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have or have had gastrointestinal ulcer; if you have bleeding in the gastrointestinal tract, the cerebral blood vessels or elsewhere; if you have a severe blood disorder, severe liver impairment, severe kidney impairment, severe heart failure or severe high blood pressure; if you have or have had bronchial asthma; if you have had asthma, urticaria or an allergic reaction to aspirin or another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic; if it is for the treatment of pain occurring before or after coronary artery bypass graft surgery (CABG); if you are 6 months or more pregnant; if you have inflammatory bowel disease such as Crohn's disease or ulcerative colitis; or if you have had gastrointestinal bleeding or perforation during treatment with a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic.

Considering the importance of the treatment, either stop breast-feeding or stop taking the medicine. Dizziness or fatigue may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery. When it is taken for a long period for an acute illness, as a rule this should be within 5 days.

Do not take it together with aspirin, another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic or high-dose methotrexate. Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you take it together with a corticosteroid, alcohol, digoxin, phenytoin, probenecid, sulfinpyrazone, a sulfonylurea, an ACE inhibitor or angiotensin II receptor antagonist, a diuretic, lithium, a coumarin anticoagulant (warfarin and the like), baclofen, an immunosuppressant (ciclosporin, tacrolimus, sirolimus), a thrombolytic, ticlopidine, an antithrombotic, a medicine that raises blood potassium (for example a potassium-sparing diuretic, an ACE inhibitor, an angiotensin II receptor antagonist, an immunosuppressant such as ciclosporin or tacrolimus, trimethoprim or heparin), an inducer of CYP2C8 or CYP2C9 (for example rifampicin or phenobarbital), low-dose methotrexate (less than 15 mg a week), an antiplatelet medicine, a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor or low-dose aspirin.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: rarely shock (chest discomfort, chills, difficulty breathing, a fall in blood pressure and the like); rarely blood disorders such as aplastic anaemia, haemolytic anaemia, granulocytopenia, leukopenia, agranulocytosis, pancytopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time) or eosinophilia; indigestion, abdominal distension, heartburn, upper abdominal pain, diarrhoea or constipation; occasionally loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain or stomach discomfort; rarely oesophagitis, oesophageal stricture, worsening of diverticula, non-specific haemorrhagic colitis, ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease, peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, bloody stools, gastritis or pancreatitis; very rarely thirst, stomatitis, erythema multiforme, systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) or hair loss; occasionally angioedema; rarely Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome); drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome) of unknown frequency; occasionally rash, urticaria, itching or purpura; rarely triggering of an asthma attack, eczema, an anaphylactic reaction or a photosensitivity reaction; rarely jaundice, raised ALT, raised AST, raised ALP, abnormal liver function or hepatitis; occasionally rhinitis, bronchospasm or acute pneumonia; rarely visual disturbance such as scotoma or dark spots, hearing loss, tinnitus or taste disturbance; fatigue, drowsiness, headache or dizziness; occasionally anxiety, restlessness, confusion or depression; rarely aseptic meningitis, severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, a stiff neck, fever or disturbance of consciousness; rarely mental disturbance, agitation, excitement, disorientation or reversible toxic amblyopia; rarely a fall or rise in blood pressure, palpitations, reduced urine output, blood in the urine, protein in the urine, raised BUN or blood creatinine, high blood potassium, reduced urine volume, generalised oedema with breathlessness or lassitude; rarely renal papillary necrosis, nephrotic syndrome, interstitial nephritis, peripheral oedema, acute pulmonary oedema, fluid retention, high blood pressure or heart failure; Conn's syndrome of unknown frequency; reduced fertility in women; occasionally swelling around the eye sockets; very rarely malaise, fever, nosebleed or worsening of inflammation.
